messages:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Pager: elevated GPU OOM rate on streaming-decode pods in us-west-2 (service: runtime-decode). Errors: CUDA OOM during token decode -> dropped requests (~5-10% error rate). Paging oncall.
ash: seeing the same in logs, OOMs spike when max_tokens high + long prefix KV cache. Repro: repeat generate with large context.
micah (oncall): I'm on it. Can someone confirm customer impact? any SLO breaches yet?
support-alex: CC'ing support - multiple customer calls reporting partial responses / truncated streams, mainly high-throughput chat flows. Severity elevated.
laura: quick mitigation idea: enforce per-request max_tokens=512 at the routing layer and enable fallback to smaller model variant. We can push a feature-flag override.
sam: agree. I can flip the emergency flag in the router. Patch below to set hard cap:
```json
{"routing_override": {"max_tokens_cap": 512, "fallback_model": "redwood-small-v1"}}
```
ash: also throttle continuous batching for the affected pool to reduce peak memory per decode. Set batch_size_max=4 temporarily.
micah (oncall): do it. Sam — flip flag and add a canary route to 10% traffic first. Post the command you run.
sam: running: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/route/override -d '{"max_tokens_cap":512, "percent":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'`
---
sre-bot: config change applied: max_tokens_cap=512 -> 10% canary at 2026-03-15T09:48:05Z.
laura: monitoring memory and error rate. Initial drop in OOMs in canary subset. Good sign.
micah (oncall): escalate plan if canary looks good: increase to 100% and enable CPU fallback policy for the rest. Also prepare container restart for worst nodes.
ash: logs show one node at 98% GPU memory and repeated decoder OOM stack trace: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating KV cache`
sam: scheduling rolling restart for pods with >5 OOMs in last 5m. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-decode -l pool=us-west-decode`
devops-bot: restart job queued for 6 nodes, draining one at a time. ETA ~4m/node.
laura: metrics: error rate from 9.3% -> 3.1% in canary after config change. Still some spikes on older sessions because existing KV caches persisted.
micah (oncall): important: mark affected customers in incident tracker. @support-alex collect list of customers who saw truncated responses and start templated notification. Use incident tag: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-DEC-STREAM.
support-alex: on it. Draft note: "We've identified a runtime OOM causing partial responses for some streaming sessions. Mitigations in progress (token caps, throttles, roll restarts). We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
ash: root cause preliminary: runaway generation from misconfigured max_tokens on some client-side retries + large prefix lengths caused KV cache growth. We need guardrails client-side and router-side.
micah (oncall): ETA for full mitigation?
laura: if all restarts go smooth and router cap rolled to 100%, expect error rate <0.5% in ~20-25m.
micah (oncall): proceeding with full rollout. Sam increase to 100% now.
sam: rolled to 100% at 2026-03-15T09:56:10Z.
---
sre-bot: full rollout applied. max_tokens_cap=512 for runtime-decode pool.
laura: after restarts and throttles, GPU OOMs reduced to baseline. Observed a ~0.2% residual error attributable to legacy sessions; terminating stale sessions helped.
micah (oncall): good. Assigning follow-ups: Ash -> implement router-side hard cap + alert if per-request KV size > threshold; Laura -> add OOM-runaway detection to runtime (pattern signature); Sam -> postmortem and customer timeline; Support-Alex -> customer notifications.
ash: will also add automated rollback to smaller model variant on first OOM detection per session.
support-alex: sent initial notifications to impacted customers.
micah (oncall): closing pager. We will keep monitoring for 2 hours. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
